A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StreamTrap study. The main text, figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison after matching reformatted material and renumbered cameras.

before.justification: v1 reports original camera-trap evaluations, adaptation experiments, loss/PEFT ablations, and deployment analyses, including Tables 1–2 and A1–A8.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, rare-species tests, and adaptation-decision analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: BioCLIP 2 adaptation with LoRA and Balanced Softmax, logit calibration, weight interpolation, historical-model selection, and adaptation-decision heuristics retain the same procedures. Expanded explanations do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 546 cameras from 17 datasets; their per-camera image, interval, and class counts match. The expanded 1,096-class vocabulary, rare-species evaluation, and temporal deployment scenarios also remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: BioCLIP 2 versus CLIP, full fine-tuning and PEFT alternatives, imbalance losses, three post-processing approaches, and adaptation-decision baselines. Newly cited methods are not added to these evaluations.

E3.justification: The reported camera subsets are revised: only four cameras overlap between the versions' 20-camera Table 1 selections. Cameras are redistributed between the main 20-camera and supplementary 50-camera comparisons, while their combined 70-camera membership remains unchanged. Training settings, splits, and metrics are retained; this does not establish rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: The loss/PEFT ablations, expanded-vocabulary and rare-species tests, failure-case analysis, post-processing study, adaptation-freezing experiment, and Adapt-or-Skip analysis are retained. Redistribution of existing camera results between figures does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Appendix D retains the same statement that a fixed splitting seed is optional rather than enforced by default.

E6.justification: For camera EFD_DCAME09, Accum accuracy changes from 71.0% in v1 Table A8, C62, to 72.3% in v2 Table 8, C38. Revised subsets also change summary results: best post-processing accuracy is 86.2% in Table A5 versus 86.7% in Table 7, which is not a same-setting gain. The r=0.907 annotation in v1 Figure 7 is absent from v2 Figure 6a. Most matched results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The TCDS definition, Balanced Softmax loss, calibration rule, and interpolation equation are unchanged. Section 5's symbolic Adapt-or-Skip formulation restates the existing higher-future-accuracy decision criterion rather than adding a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: fixed-site temporal recognition, StreamTrap, adaptation difficulties from imbalance and temporal shifts, practical adaptation recipes, and unresolved deployment decisions.

C2.justification: v2 characterizes the MSP–accuracy relationship as moderate and softens continued adaptation's benefits from compounding improvements to potentially cumulative, uneven gains. Section 4.4 explicitly calls future-label model selection non-deployable and diagnostic. The broader upper-bound caveat, failure mechanisms, and limitations already existed.

D1.justification: The camera index changes B04's dataset attribution from Snapshot Paarl Mtn in v1 Table A9 to Snapshot Pilanesberg in v2 Table 10, aligning it with the benchmark's dataset listing. Training hyperparameters, validation procedures, preprocessing instructions, and the project URL are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including C-Flat, AVA-Bench, a robotics continual-learning survey, and test-time adaptation works, while removing De Lange et al.'s continual-learning survey. The substantive positioning around fixed-site temporal recognition remains stable; other reference edits include deduplication and metadata changes.

P1.justification: Extensive paragraph rewriting throughout the introduction, related work, and Sections 3–5 substantially revises the exposition. Heading conventions, appendix references, and the Adapt-or-Skip explanation are revised, although the overall scientific narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, with widespread resizing and relocation. v1 Figures 2–3 become v2 Figure 2, Figures 7–8 become Figure 6, protocol diagrams are redrawn, and post-processing plots and appendix tables are reorganized. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Clearer exposition and explicit diagnostic upper-bound wording improve accessibility. However, v2 Table 7 retains an obsolete 87.6% Oracle caption beside an updated 87.0% entry, and several figures and the complete-results table become appreciably smaller. With the underlying evidence largely retained, these opposing clarity and reporting/readability effects do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
